exams.syllabus: Trinity Piano / Electronic Keyboard & Organ syllabus. Lists read from the board's official repertoire pages.
comps: Face-to-face: 3 pieces at 22 each (66; fluency & accuracy 7, technical facility 7, communication & interpretation 8) + technical work 14 + supporting tests 20 = 100. Keyboard technical work: keyboard exercise (G1-8; none at Initial) then scales & chord knowledge or exercises; organ: scales (G1), scales & arpeggios (G2-5), plus pedal study at G6-8. Supporting tests: Initial-G5 any two of sight reading, aural, improvisation, musical knowledge (10 each); G6-8 sight reading (10) plus aural or improvisation (10). Distinction 87-100, Merit 75-86, Pass 60-74, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44; per piece D 19-22, M 16-18, P 13-15. No need to pass every section. UCAS points G6 8/10/12, G7 12/14/16, G8 18/24/30 (pass/merit/distinction). Digital technical-work pathway: 3 pieces at 22 (66) + technical work 14 + overall performance 20 = 100; no supporting tests; choose scales/chords (or scales & arpeggios for organ) set A or B, or two exercises (keyboard). Digital repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces at 25 each = 100.

Electronic Keyboard: 3 pieces from the repertoire list; own composition may replace one (Initial-G5); at G6-8 also own-choice piece or own arrangement (keyboard or non-keyboard, of similar demand, not pre-approved). Each graded book has one own-interpretation option (candidate chooses voices/style; auto intros/endings not allowed). Single-fingered or fully fingered chords allowed; efficient set-up expected. Organ: 3 pieces in groups A and B, at least one from each; own composition may replace one; prepare in full, observe short repeats only. Own composition lengths 0.5-1 min at Initial to 3.5-5 min at G8; stave notation G6-8. Memory optional; no metronome.

Digital exams are filmed in one continuous take and uploaded. Technical-work pathway: 3 pieces, technical work (keyboard exercise then scales/chords set A or B or two exercises; organ scales & arpeggios set A or B plus pedal study at G6-8), overall performance mark, no supporting tests. Repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces. Own composition allowed.
sections: No keyboard exercise. Scales & chord knowledge from memory, piano voice, hands separately, one octave, legato mf, min q=60: C major, A minor, C major and A minor pentatonics, chromatic from D; triads of C major and A minor (RH or LH). Or exercises (music may be used): prepare all three (keyboard functions, scalic, pianistic); candidate picks one, examiner one of the other two.
Approx 1 grade lower; 30 s prep after set-up; single-fingered chords with rhythm/accompaniment or fully fingered chords without rhythm (to G5). C major, 2/4, crotchets/minims, mf, 5-finger position.

Choose two of: sight reading, aural, improvisation, musical knowledge. Aural (4-bar major melody): clap pulse on 3rd playing; forte/piano; legato/staccato; highest or lowest of first 3 notes. Improv (stylistic/motivic/harmonic): 4 bars, C major, chords I, V. Musical knowledge (on own pieces): note names, durations, clefs, signatures, basic terms.

Keyboard technical work: keyboard exercise (G1-8; none at Initial) then scales & chord knowledge or exercises; organ: scales (G1), scales & arpeggios (G2-5), plus pedal study at G6-8. Supporting tests: Initial-G5 any two of sight reading, aural, improvisation, musical knowledge (10 each); G6-8 sight reading (10) plus aural or improvisation (10). Distinction 87-100, Merit 75-86, Pass 60-74, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44; per piece D 19-22, M 16-18, P 13-15. No need to pass every section. UCAS points G6 8/10/12, G7 12/14/16, G8 18/24/30 (pass/merit/distinction). Digital technical-work pathway: 3 pieces at 22 (66) + technical work 14 + overall performance 20 = 100; no supporting tests; choose scales/chords (or scales & arpeggios for organ) set A or B, or two exercises (keyboard). Digital repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces at 25 each = 100.

Electronic Keyboard: 3 pieces from the repertoire list; own composition may replace one (Initial-G5); at G6-8 also own-choice piece or own arrangement (keyboard or non-keyboard, of similar demand, not pre-approved). Each graded book has one own-interpretation option (candidate chooses voices/style; auto intros/endings not allowed). Single-fingered or fully fingered chords allowed; efficient set-up expected. Organ: 3 pieces in groups A and B, at least one from each; own composition may replace one; prepare in full, observe short repeats only. Own composition lengths 0.5-1 min at Initial to 3.5-5 min at G8; stave notation G6-8. Memory optional; no metronome.
None. No theory or lower-grade prerequisite; each grade assumes confidence in earlier requirements. Organ has no Initial grade (starts at Grade 1).

Digital exams are filmed in one continuous take and uploaded. Technical-work pathway: 3 pieces, technical work (keyboard exercise then scales/chords set A or B or two exercises; organ scales & arpeggios set A or B plus pedal study at G6-8), overall performance mark, no supporting tests. Repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces. Own composition allowed.
sections: Keyboard exercise from memory: scale + arpeggio from centres Ab/G#, B or C. Scales & chords from memory, two octaves, min q=130: same patterns on Ab/G#, B, C; pentatonics, chromatic from any note, blues; 6th, diminished 7th, augmented chords; 7th and minor 7th chords with all inversions. Or exercises (music may be used): prepare any three of four (keyboard functions, scalic, pianistic, sequencing with pre-recorded part); candidate picks one, examiner one other.
E, Ab major, F minor, 2/2, minor 7ths on black roots, major 7ths, dotted semibreves.

Sight reading plus aural or improvisation. Aural (8-bar harmonised): as G6 with modulation to subdominant/dominant/relative key and three changes (pitch in melody, rhythm). Improv: 16 bars, E/Ab major.

p0625.d: Sunny, spirited opening movement of the G major concerto, with quick passagework, operatic lyricism and a cadenza.

s1070.d: Easy arrangement of the famous Jupiter melody from The Planets; broad and noble, practising legato and a warm tone.

s1390.d: Arrangement of 'Memory' from Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical Cats (1981): a famous, slow, building ballad suiting a singing cello tone.

s1810.d: A simple arrangement of the tender Rodgers & Hammerstein waltz from The Sound of Music. Practises smooth legato and gentle triple time.
s1810.rw: Much-loved tune; easy to play musically

s2207.d: The 'Skye Boat Song', a lilting Scottish boat song in 6/8. Practises smooth legato, steady rocking rhythm and gentle phrasing.
s2207.rw: Beautiful melody; easy to make musical

s2237.d: Arrangement of the Jamaican folk song with its lively, syncopated calypso rhythm. Practises rhythmic precision and bright, lifted articulation.

s0382.d: Brahms's Hungarian Dance no. 5 (1869): fiery minor-key tune, sudden tempo shifts and Hungarian flair. Needs rhythmic bite and stylish rubato.

w04020.d: Parry's setting 'Jerusalem'; a majestic hymn tune that practises long phrases and a sustained line.

w04084.d: Arrangement of the famous Swan Lake quartet of cygnets, a quick staccato dance; practises light, precise articulation and coordination.

w04188.d: Galway's arrangement of Handel's Queen of Sheba; brilliant, rhythmic and festive; practises fast articulation and bright tone.

w04407.d: Arrangement of Cherubino's aria Voi che sapete from The Marriage of Figaro (1786). Practises lyrical phrasing and breath planning.

w04682.d: Arrangement of the popular English tune English Country Garden; simple folk style.

w05581.d: Arrangement of the Disney song 'A Whole New World' from Aladdin (1992), by Alan Menken. Lyrical; practises smooth phrasing.

w06004.d: Jazz arrangement of Jobim's 1962 bossa nova classic; practises melodic phrasing, swing feel and tasteful embellishment.

w06105.d: Jazz arrangement of Erskine Hawkins' 1939 big-band hit; practises melodic phrasing, swing feel and tasteful embellishment.

w06434.d: Fats Waller's swing standard arranged for brass solo. Practises relaxed swing feel, jazz articulation and light phrasing.

w06559.d: Over the Sea to Skye, Scottish folk tune in this arrangement. Practises lyrical phrasing, legato and steady tempo.

w06582.d: Walking in the Air from The Snowman in this arrangement. Practises long legato phrases, soft dynamics and shaping.

w06620.d: Feelings, the popular Latin ballad by Albert and Gasté, arranged in Latin style. Practises lyrical phrasing, expression and smooth legato.

w06902.d: Clara's lullaby that opens Porgy and Bess (1935), in A minor: slow, bluesy and rocking. Demands sustained high lines, relaxed jazz inflection and long breaths.

w07234.d: Arrangement of the Irish jig The Irish Washerwoman practising fast compound rhythm and articulation.

v00144.d: Arrangement of the Sound of Music song teaching the do-re-mi scale, bright and recognisable. Practises scale patterns and rhythmic accuracy.

v00279.d: Classic Disney song from Pinocchio, a slow lyrical ballad with a floating line. Practises legato, breath control and gentle expression.

v00342.d: Scottish folk song Wild Mountain Thyme, with a lilting, romantic melody. Practises smooth legato and expressive, flowing phrasing.

v00346.d: Traditional Irish ballad about Molly Malone. Flowing, waltz-like tune practising legato and storytelling.

v00419.d: Bert's haunting waltz-like song from Mary Poppins (1964), built on a minor-key melody. Practises legato, rubato and rhythmic lilt.

v00478.d: Scottish folk song Ye Banks and Braes (Bonnie Doon), words by Robert Burns. Lyrical and melancholy; practises legato and expressive phrasing.

v00481.d: Scottish Jacobite song Charlie Is My Darling, lively and rhythmic. Practises Scots character, clear diction and spirited delivery.

v00614.d: Arrangement of the hymn 'Amazing Grace' (John Newton, 1779). A simple, rising melody practising long phrases and sincere expression.

v00673.d: Arrangement of Justin Hurwitz's jazz-influenced score for La La Land (2016). Swinging piano style, syncopation and bright harmony.

v01505.d: Dowland's famous lute-song lament 'Flow, My Tears' (Lachrimae), a slow pavan-like song with sustained melancholy line and ornament.

v01959.d: Brahms's famous Lullaby arranged for electronic keyboard with auto-accompaniment; practises smooth melody and gentle registration.

v01960.d: Rock-and-roll original with driving beat and bright voices; practises rhythm and chord accompaniment.

v01961.d: Largo theme from Dvořák's New World Symphony arranged for keyboard; practises sustained melody and expressive registration.

v01962.d: American folk tune 'Little Brown Jug', cheerful with a jaunty beat; practises rhythm and left-hand chord changes.

v01963.d: Theme from Titanic ('My Heart Will Go On', James Horner and Will Jennings, 1997) arranged for keyboard; practises melody and accompaniment styles.

v01964.d: Queen's 1975 epic 'Bohemian Rhapsody' arranged in simplified keyboard form; practises melody lines and changing styles.

v01965.d: Theme from Mozart's opera Don Giovanni arranged for keyboard; practises clear melody and orchestral voices.

v01966.d: Dolly Parton's 1973 country hit 'Jolene', arranged for keyboard; practises melody and rhythmic accompaniment.

v01967.d: Song 'Little Buttercup' from Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore (1878), arranged for keyboard; practises lively melody and rhythm.

v01968.d: American folk song 'Home on the Range' in a basic version for keyboard; practises melody and simple chords.

v01969.d: English folk song 'Lavender Blue' arranged for keyboard; practises gentle melody and accompaniment.

v01970.d: Spiritual 'Michael Row the Boat Ashore' with own interpretation, choosing voices and accompaniment; practises style and rhythm.

v01971.d: Opening of Vivaldi's Spring from The Four Seasons, arranged for keyboard; practises lively rhythm and clear articulation.

v01972.d: Theme from Beethoven's Pastoral Symphony arranged for keyboard; practises lyrical melody and steady accompaniment.

v01973.d: Cheerful easy piano piece from Piano Time Pieces, here for keyboard; practises light rhythm and steady pulse.

v01974.d: Elgar's 'Land of Hope and Glory' from Pomp and Circumstance March no. 1, arranged for keyboard; practises march rhythm and full-sounding chords.

v01975.d: Rock-and-roll classic 'Rock Around the Clock' (1954) arranged for keyboard; practises rock-and-roll rhythm and accompaniment.

v01976.d: James Hook's Gavotte in lively Classical style, from Piano Time Pieces; practises clear articulation and dance rhythm.

v01977.d: Song 'Summer Nights' from the musical Grease (1971), arranged for keyboard in Latin style; practises style and chord changes.

v01978.d: Leiber and Stoller's rock-and-roll song, made famous by Elvis Presley in Jailhouse Rock (1957), arranged for keyboard; practises rhythm and style changes.

v01979.d: Kenny Loggins's 1984 hit 'Footloose', with own interpretation; practises upbeat rhythm and accompaniment choice.

v01980.d: Theme from Schubert's 'Unfinished' Symphony no. 8 arranged for keyboard; practises sustained lyrical lines and expressive registration.

v01981.d: Original piece for electronic keyboard evoking spinning dervishes with a repetitive, hypnotic pattern. Builds steady rhythm and use of auto-accompaniment at an entry level.

v01982.d: Sting's gentle 1993 ballad arranged for keyboard. Melody over simple chordal accompaniment; practises smooth legato and steady rhythm.

v01983.d: Arrangement of the Velvet Underground's jangly 1967 song 'There She Goes Again'. Steady rock rhythm with simple chords and a catchy melody.

v01984.d: The Shaker melody 'Simple Gifts' style dance-hymn arranged for keyboard. Simple, bright tune over a basic accompaniment; practises clear phrasing and steady pulse.

v01985.d: Traditional Irish tune about the beautiful Mourne coast, in lively jig-like rhythm. Practises rhythmic drive and basic auto-accompaniment control.

v01986.d: ABBA's 1980 power ballad arranged for keyboard. Expressive melody over sustained chords; asks for steady pulse and sensitive dynamics.

v01987.d: Burgmüller's flowing minor-key study from the 25 Easy and Progressive Studies, arranged for keyboard. Practises quick, even right-hand figures and light staccato.

v01988.d: Handel's familiar Air from Water Music, to be played with the candidate's own registration and interpretation. Gracious melody practising phrasing and style choices.

v01989.d: Quiet original piece with a gently walking melody. Practises legato phrasing and smooth accompaniment changes.

v01990.d: Bob Merrill's 1950s novelty song in mambo rhythm, arranged for keyboard. Lively Latin groove practising rhythm styles and fills.

v01991.d: Christopher Norton's Microjazz piece in a jazzy, syncopated style. Practises off-beat rhythms and crisp chordal accompaniment.

v01992.d: Title song from the 1968 film musical by the Sherman brothers. Bouncy tune with playful character; practises rhythm and accompaniment style.

v01993.d: Johann Strauss II's waltz 'Du und du' ('You and You') from Die Fledermaus, arranged for keyboard. Waltz accompaniment with a flowing tune.

v01994.d: Famous Scottish march tune arranged for keyboard. Dotted rhythms and strong pulse practise marching style and registration.

v01995.d: Consuelo Velazquez's 1940 bolero, a classic love song. Slow Latin groove with expressive melody; practises style and chord changes.

v01996.d: Mariah Carey's 1993 power ballad arranged for keyboard. Sustained melody and building chords; asks for dynamic shaping and stamina.

v01997.d: Bach's serene Arioso from Cantata 156, famous as a slow melody over gentle continuo. Practises long legato phrases and ornament shaping.

v01998.d: Original keyboard piece with relaxed, breezy Latin-flavoured style. Practises syncopation and accompaniment patterns.

v01999.d: Traditional American fiddle tune, lively and repetitive. Practises fast, rhythmic accompaniment and bright registration.

v02000.d: Kander's Broadway/Sinatra anthem. Big swing style tune with brassy chords; practises swing feel and building energy.

v02001.d: Beatles hit from 1968 with boogie-style piano riff and bluesy chords. Practises rock rhythm and left-hand patterns.

v02002.d: Beatles song from Sgt. Pepper (1967), music-hall flavoured and witty. Practises light swing feel and clear melody.

v02003.d: Giorgio Moroder's 1984 film theme song, synth-pop in character. Driving pulse with a soaring melody; fits electronic keyboard sounds well.

v02004.d: Christopher Norton's jazzy original, perhaps with unusual metre. Practises rhythmic precision and chord colour.

v02005.d: Procol Harum's 1967 hit with its Bach-inspired organ line. Slow, soulful tune practising sustained chords and expressive phrasing.

v02006.d: Rodgers & Hammerstein's gentle song from The King and I. Waltz-like flow practising legato melody and smooth accompaniment.

v02007.d: Scottish pipe lament, a slow air about leaving Lochaber. Plaintive melody practising expression and ornamental touches.

v02008.d: Irish traditional tune played with the candidate's own interpretation. Lively or lilting dance feel; practises ornaments and registration choices.

v02009.d: Duet-style ballad from the musical Chess by Benny Andersson with lyrics by Tim Rice. Powerful, sustained melody practising dynamics and chord control.

v02010.d: Hans Zimmer and Klaus Badelt's swashbuckling theme from the 2003 film. Driving minor-key ostinato practising rhythmic drive and orchestral registration.

v02011.d: Famous triumphant finale theme of Beethoven's Fifth Symphony, arranged for keyboard. Bold chords and fanfare character.

v02012.d: Theme from the slow movement of Beethoven's Pathétique Sonata, a hymn-like melody. Practises cantabile line and sustained accompaniment.

v02013.d: Jobim's classic bossa nova ('Off Key') from 1959. Gently syncopated groove with chromatic harmony practising Latin style and chord voicings.

v02014.d: Scott Joplin's 1903 ragtime piece, arranged for keyboard. Syncopated melody over oom-pah bass; practises rag style and coordination.

v02015.d: American hymn ('My life flows on') by Robert Lowry, arranged for keyboard. Simple tune with steady accompaniment; practises phrasing and registration.

v02016.d: Original keyboard study using fourths in melody and chord shapes. Practises interval reading and rhythmic accuracy.

v02017.d: Upbeat, joyful original with gospel or fanfare feel. Practises rhythm and bright registration.

v02018.d: Finale number from the musical Hairspray (2002). Energetic dance beat practising driving rhythm and accompaniment style.

v02019.d: Original keyboard piece of tense, careful character suggested by the title. Practises rhythmic precision and dynamics.

v02020.d: Lively polka arranged for keyboard. Bouncy two-beat rhythm practising crisp staccato and steady pulse.

v02021.d: African-American spiritual with the candidate's own interpretation. Bluesy tune practising rhythmic freedom and style choices.

v02022.d: Wagner's famous orchestral Ride of the Valkyries, arranged for keyboard. Galloping rhythms and brass-like fanfares.

v02023.d: Kenny Dorham's 1963 jazz standard, played with the candidate's interpretation. Latin groove, minor-key melody and jazz chord changes.

v02024.d: Original ragtime-style piece with syncopated melody. Practises rag rhythms and left-hand patterns.

v02025.d: Christopher Norton's ragtime-flavoured piece with mechanical, driving energy. Practises syncopation and coordination.

v02026.d: Original tango with dramatic rhythms and minor harmonies. Practises tango style, accents and dynamics.

v02027.d: Theme from Rossini's 1817 overture, a brisk tune over snare-drum rhythms. Practises crisp articulation and fast passages.

v02028.d: Sousa's 1889 march, arranged for keyboard. Bold melodies and oom-pah accompaniment practising march style and stamina.

v02029.d: Johann Strauss II's waltz (Frühlingsstimmen) of 1882. Sparkling melody and waltz accompaniment practising rubato and agility.

v02030.d: Waltz from Tchaikovsky's 1880 Serenade for Strings, arranged for keyboard. Graceful lilting melody with rich harmony.

v02031.d: African-American spiritual with long, singing melody. Practises legato phrasing and rich chords.

v02032.d: Traditional tune about the fiddler Hardiman, likely an Irish dance. Lively, ornamented melody practising dance rhythm.

v02033.d: Medley of Scottish jigs arranged for keyboard. Fast compound rhythm and switching tunes; practises stamina and drive.

v02034.d: Chopin's lyrical Romanze (second movement) from his Piano Concerto no. 1, arranged for keyboard. Expressive melody over flowing accompaniment.

v02035.d: Jelly Roll Morton's 1923 jazz classic, an early swing/stomp piece. Syncopated rhythm practising jazz style and stamina.

v02036.d: Original samba with lively Latin percussion-driven groove. Practises syncopation and rhythmic stamina.

v02037.d: Medley of Celtic tunes played with the candidate's own interpretation. Jigs and reels mixed with slower airs; practises ornament and style.

v02038.d: Earth, Wind & Fire's 1978 funk-disco hit. Syncopated groove and bright brass-style riffs; needs rhythmic precision.

v02039.d: Bach's famed organ Toccata and Fugue, arranged for electronic keyboard. Dramatic opening gestures, fast figuration and fugue.

v02040.d: Sheryl Crow's 1997 James Bond theme, with candidate's own interpretation. Sultry, driving rock-pop style.

v02041.d: Philip Glass's minimalist piece from the film The Hours (2002). Repeating arpeggios and slow harmonic shifts demand evenness and stamina.

v02042.d: Original lyrical keyboard piece with romantic flowing harmony. Practises expressive phrasing and registration.

v02043.d: Mendelssohn's well-known Wedding March from A Midsummer Night's Dream, arranged for keyboard. Fanfares and processional character.

v02044.d: Traditional-style Irish or Scottish reel with the title suggesting shifting rhythms. Fast tune demands precision and stamina.

v02045.d: Dizzy Gillespie's 1942 bebop standard with exotic Afro-Cuban feel. Fast improvised-style lines and jazz harmony.

v02046.d: Percy Grainger's 'In Dahomey', a cakewalk with ragtime flavour. Syncopated, sparkling character and busy textures.

v02047.d: Liszt's vivid Friska from Hungarian Rhapsody no. 2, arranged for keyboard. Furious, virtuosic finale with gypsy-style dance rhythms.

v02048.d: Paganini's famous Caprice 24 theme and variations, arranged for keyboard. Virtuoso variations of speed and dexterity.

v02049.d: Original lively dance piece for keyboard. Practises rhythmic drive and fast figures.

v02050.d: Bill Whelan's Irish dance showpiece from 1994, arranged for keyboard. Driving rhythms, big climaxes and folk-style melodies.

v02051.d: Widor's famous Toccata from Organ Symphony no. 5, arranged for keyboard. Rapid repeated chords over a pedal melody.

z00405.d: Arrangement of Handel's slow, stately Sarabande, with a noble D minor theme. Practises dignified phrasing, chordal accompaniment and steady triple time on keyboard.

z00406.d: Arrangement of the famous opening of Mozart's Eine kleine Nachtmusik. Practises crisp rhythm, clear chords and light, lively articulation on electronic keyboard.

z00407.d: Arrangement of Bach's chorale 'Jesu, Joy of Man's Desiring' with its flowing triplet accompaniment. Practises smooth lines, registration and balance between melody and accompaniment.

z00408.d: Arrangement of Chopin's Minute Waltz, a brilliant, fast piece with a running right hand. Practises quick finger work, even rhythm and clear style on electronic keyboard.
